message.content: A common example of a multinucleated cell is a **syncytium** (plural syncytia). Syncytial cells arise when several individual cells fuse together into one larger cell containing many nuclei within a shared cytoplasm. This process occurs naturally during muscle development—forming skeletal and cardiac myocytes—and in certain pathological conditions such as viral infections where infected cells merge.
